description:
Make the digest of a gate's declared inputs the only way a gate verdict is reused, removing the commit-based "already passed at HEAD" skip and the dirty-tree flag that jit's own tracker writes falsify.

## Background

Two mechanisms avoid re-running an automated checker:

1. A commit-based skip: an evaluation is skipped when the latest run passed at the current `HEAD` commit. Each run records `commit`, `branch` and `tree_dirty`; `tree_dirty` comes from `git status --porcelain` over the whole worktree.
2. Digest reuse: a gate declaring `[gates.inputs]` digests those files' working-tree content and reuses any prior verdict over the same digest, across issues.

The commit-based skip breaks in normal use. Every gate evaluation writes the tracker's own files, so the next run records `tree_dirty: true`, and committing those files moves `HEAD`, so the next evaluation re-runs a ten-minute checker over an unchanged tree. An execution lead ends up alternating gate, commit, gate, and avoiding commits while a gate runs. Digest reuse already answers the same question exactly, independent of commits.

Declaring whole-repository inputs is also awkward: `.` is rejected as a root, so a checker that scans the whole repository must list every top-level entry, and a new top-level directory silently escapes the digest. A data root nested in the worktree is digested whenever a root covers it, so tracker writes change the digest unless every gate excludes it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An automated gate that declares no inputs executes its checker on every evaluation; no commit-based skip exists, and its `already_passed` output field is removed.
- [hard] REQ-02: Gate-run records carry no dirty-tree field; nothing reads or writes it.
- [hard] REQ-03: `.` is accepted as an input root and covers the whole worktree minus declared exclusions.
- [hard] REQ-04: The input digest never includes a data root nested in the worktree, in the same way it never includes `.git`; tracker writes during an evaluation leave every digest unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-05: `--force` executes the checker unconditionally, and its help text describes only digest reuse.
- [hard] REQ-06: User documentation describes one reuse mechanism, and the net change removes more code than it adds.

## Notes

- Supersedes `ea2bb1f6` (refuse to re-run a passed gate without `--force`): with one reuse mechanism, re-evaluating unchanged inputs is free and `--force` remains the deliberate re-run.
- A checker that reads git state (the `HEAD` tree or the index) rather than working-tree files is outside what a digest can see; the gate documentation states that inputs describe working-tree content.
title: Reuse gate verdicts only by declared-input digest
